Messages.Author: Brian Roberson
Messages.Body:
Does Force of Will count for No Repeat Action? I know that you no longer
untap, but can a tapped vampire who bled play Force of Will and bleed again?

Brian Roberson
BTW, I tied for 2nd at the tournament in Pleasanton, CA with a weenie
presence/dominate deck.

Messages.Author: TheLa...@hotmail.com
Messages.Body:
In article <Cdwx2.1279$yv3...@news.rdc1.sfba.home.com>,

"Brian Roberson" <jrob...@home.com> wrote:
> Does Force of Will count for No Repeat Action? I know that you no longer
> untap, but can a tapped vampire who bled play Force of Will and bleed again?

A vampire that has bled (successfully or not) cannot play Force of Will
on the same turn if you are playing with the tournament rules that
prohibit repeat actions.

If you are simply playing the game, only Obedience prevents you from
taking a specific action again.

Carpe Noctem.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
TheLa...@hotmail.com wrote:
>
> In article <Cdwx2.1279$yv3...@news.rdc1.sfba.home.com>,
> "Brian Roberson" <jrob...@home.com> wrote:
> > Does Force of Will count for No Repeat Action? I know that you no longer
> > untap, but can a tapped vampire who bled play Force of Will and bleed again?
>
> A vampire that has bled (successfully or not) cannot play Force of Will
> on the same turn if you are playing with the tournament rules that
> prohibit repeat actions.

Correct. A tapped bleed action is still a bleed action type.

> If you are simply playing the game, only Obedience prevents you from
> taking a specific action again.

Both Obedience and Change of Target restrict the acting minion's
choices - but by specific action, not by action type.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <Cdwx2.1279$yv3...@news.rdc1.sfba.home.com>, Brian Roberson

<jrob...@home.com> writes

>Does Force of Will count for No Repeat Action?

Yes. It is an action, no more, no less.

> I know that you no longer
>untap, but can a tapped vampire who bled play Force of Will and bleed again?

No. He has already bled, so he cannot bleed again. NRA cares not for
tapped/untapped status.
